about: Per-coupling documentation for E6 decision cards. Oracles and cards read it; agents never see it. 'contract' is the bean that changes the shared contract (the arena's coupling notes for the designed pairs; the measured merge for the natural ones). 'winner' is the per-coupling (table) oracle's documented choice, a product owner's call, with 'rationale'. 'texts' holds the decision line for each possible winner. 'adapt' lists winners whose decision keeps both contracts (the arriving bean adapts; nothing is reverted). 'contradiction': false means both canonical suites can pass together.

pairs.contract_note: paginate() returns { items, total } instead of an array; GET /invoices returned paginate()'s result as its body.

specs.t002: paginate() returns { items, total }; list endpoints send x-total-count and keep plain array bodies
specs.t022: GET /invoices returns the caller's invoices as a JSON array, newest first, filtered by status and paged

pairs.rationale: Not a contradiction: both specs hold when the new caller sends page.items.

texts.t002: paginate() returns { items, total } (t002). Every list endpoint keeps a plain JSON array body, so GET /invoices returns page.items, newest first; it may also send x-total-count like the other lists.
texts.t022: GET /invoices returns a plain JSON array (t022). paginate() now returns { items, total } (t002), so the invoice list sends page.items as its body.

pairs.contract_note: formatMoney groups thousands ($1,000.00); the plain-text invoice test pins $1000.00.

specs.t005: Displayed amounts group thousands: formatMoney prints $1,000.00 (amounts under $1,000 unchanged)
specs.t031: The plain-text invoice prints its amounts as $1000.00, using the shop's normal currency formatting

pairs.rationale: t031's own prompt says its amounts use the shop's normal currency formatting, which t005 changes; one money format everywhere.

texts.t005: Money is shown with thousands separators everywhere, the plain-text invoice included, because it uses the shop's normal currency formatting: '1 x <item> - $1,000.00', 'Subtotal: $1,000.00', 'Total: $1,065.00'. Amounts under $1,000 look as before.
texts.t031: The plain-text invoice prints amounts without thousands separators ($1000.00) so they paste cleanly into expense tools; everywhere else money is grouped by formatMoney (t005).

pairs.contract_note: trackingNumber moves from Order to Shipment; the shipped-email template read order.trackingNumber.

specs.t011: The tracking number belongs to the shipment: Shipment.trackingNumber, and orders no longer carry one
specs.t018: The 'order shipped' email adds a line 'Tracking number: <number>'

pairs.rationale: Not a contradiction: the email can read the number from the shipment.

texts.t011: The tracking number lives on the shipment, not the order (t011). The shipped email reads it from the order's shipment and still shows 'Tracking number: <number>' (t018).
texts.t018: The shipped email must show 'Tracking number: <number>' (t018); since the number moved to the shipment (t011), the email reads it from the shipment.

pairs.contract_note: Tax is rounded once per rate over the invoice and spread over the lines; the refund test pins three identical $3.33 lines to $3.76 each.

specs.t023: Tax is rounded once per rate over the invoice and spread over its lines (43c, 43c and 44c on three $3.33 lines at 13%)
specs.t036: A line refund is its net less its discount share plus its tax, so three identical lines refund identically ($3.76 each)

pairs.rationale: Matching the tax authority's figure is a legal requirement; refunds must return the tax actually charged, so identical lines may differ by a cent.

texts.t023: Tax follows the tax authority: rounded once per rate and spread over the lines (t023). A line refund returns that line's net, less its share of the discount, plus the tax actually charged on that line, so identical lines can differ by a cent (two refunds of $3.76 and one of $3.77 in the three-line example), and refunding every line still returns the invoice total.
texts.t036: Identical invoice lines must carry identical tax so that they refund identically (t036), so invoices keep rounding tax per line. applyRateToTotal may exist in lib/money.ts as a helper, but invoice line taxes are not spread.

pairs.contract_note: Order.total now includes shipping; the signature test's order sits just under the $250 threshold without shipping ($249.21).

specs.t028: A delivery needs a signature when order.total is at least $250; $234.00 of goods plus tax ($249.21) does not
specs.t032: Order.total is the full amount payable: goods after discount, plus tax, plus shipping

pairs.rationale: A parcel's worth is its goods, not the delivery fee: the signature rule keeps comparing goods plus tax, and Order.total still includes shipping. Both specs hold; no test changes.

texts.t028: Order.total includes shipping (t032), and the signature rule compares the parcel's worth with the threshold: goods after discount plus tax, without shipping (order.total minus order.shippingCost). An order of $234.00 plus tax ($249.21 of goods) needs no signature.
texts.t032: Order.total is the full amount payable, shipping included (t032), and the signature rule compares that total with the threshold, so a $234.00 order plus tax and shipping needs a signature; an example just under the threshold uses $230.00 of goods.

pairs.contract_note: Order.total now includes shipping; the confirmation-email test of thousands grouping pins the old total ($42.60 for a $40.00 US order).

specs.t005: The order confirmation shows grouped amounts; a $40.00 US order's email reads 'Total: $42.60' (goods plus tax)
specs.t032: The confirmation email shows the new order total, shipping included ('Total: $111.50' for a $100.00 US order)

pairs.rationale: Customers complained the email total was lower than what they pay; t032 fixes that and t005's test only pinned the old total by example.

texts.t032: The confirmation email shows the new order total, shipping included (t032), formatted with thousands separators (t005): a $40.00 order to the US reads 'Total: $47.60' when it pays $5.00 shipping.
texts.t005: The confirmation email keeps showing goods plus tax as its total ('Total: $42.60' for a $40.00 order); the shipping-inclusive Order.total (t032) is not printed in the email.

pairs.contract_note: Standard shipping becomes free from $75.00 of goods; the order-total tests use $100.00 orders that pay $5.00 shipping.

specs.t032: Order.total adds shipping; a $100.00 US order pays $5.00 shipping and totals $111.50
specs.t033: Standard shipping is free when the goods come to $75.00 or more

pairs.rationale: Free shipping is a pricing decision by marketing; t032's examples only assumed a shipping charge on a $100.00 order.

texts.t033: Standard shipping is free from $75.00 of goods (t033), and Order.total includes whatever shipping is charged (t032): a $100.00 US order pays no shipping and totals $106.50; examples that need a shipping charge use orders under $75.00.
texts.t032: t032's accepted totals stand: a $100.00 US order pays $5.00 standard shipping. Free standard shipping (t033) only starts above the order values those examples use.

pairs.contract_note: Both rewrite how invoice tax is computed: a federal/regional breakdown versus once-per-rate rounding spread over lines.

specs.t003: Invoices carry taxBreakdown { federal, regional } that always adds up to the invoice tax
specs.t023: Tax is rounded once per rate over the invoice and spread over its lines

pairs.rationale: Not a contradiction: the breakdown can be derived from the spread tax and still add up.

texts.t023: Tax is rounded once per rate and spread over the lines (t023); the federal/regional breakdown (t003) is computed from those amounts and still adds up to the invoice tax.
texts.t003: The invoice carries the federal/regional breakdown (t003), and it must add up to the invoice tax as computed by the once-per-rate rounding (t023).
